# AI Engineering Compiler v0.6.1

A documentation release. Nothing the compiler generates changes, so there is
nothing to re-sync.

## The threat model covers `security: hardened`

[`docs/threat-model.md`](https://github.com/akin-oz/ai-engineering/blob/v0.6.1/docs/threat-model.md)
now treats the 0.6.0 preset the way it treats each layer:

- **What it turns on:** `Read` deny rules for `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, and
  `*.key`, and the sandbox, so those rules also bind shell commands.
- **What the compiler guarantees:** your own blocks still apply and deny still
  wins; a sandbox value that conflicts with the preset is an error; Codex and
  Cursor gaps are never accepted on your behalf; a later change to the preset
  shows up as drift until you re-sync.
- **What it does not cover:** secrets under other names, network access, the
  tools that run outside the sandbox, and machines where the sandbox cannot
  run.

The attack table now says where the preset is what turns the sandbox on, and
adds a row for secrets stored under other filenames.

## Corrections

- `aie audit` reads `.claude/settings.json` as it is on disk, uncommitted edits
  included. It reports an empty deny list, a disabled sandbox, and secret files
  that no rule covers; it does not check the preset's rules one by one. The
  README and threat model said "committed settings" and implied more.
- Only a conflicting sandbox value is an error next to the preset. Allowing a
  rule the preset denies has always synced with a `permission-conflict`
  warning; the docs now say so.
